newsitem.title: GERMANY: Steffi Graf's father may leave prison, court says.
newsitem.headline: Steffi Graf's father may leave prison, court says.

text.p: A German court trying the father of tennis star Steffi Graf on tax evasion charges ruled on Friday he could be released from custody on bail, but prosecutors immediately objected to the decision.
It was not immediately clear if Peter Graf would be free to go while a higher court decided on the prosecutors' objection.
A court in Mannheim, southwestern Germany, set bail for Graf at five million marks ($3.32 million). It also said he would have to report to police twice a week and receive pyschotherapy.
Graf's mental health during more than a year in investigative custody has been the subject of German newspaper speculation.
After a brief recess, the judges rejected a prosecution argument that Graf could not go free until the higher court had decided on their objection.

This raised the prospect that Graf could be freed at least until the higher court's decision if he manages to post bail in time. There was no indication of how quickly the higher court would make its judgment.
Graf is accused of evading 19 million marks ($12.61 million) of tax on his daughter's earnings between 1989 and 1993.
Former family tax adviser Joachim Eckardt is also on trial. The court said Eckardt could be freed on bail of 300,000 marks ($199,100).

Graf was taken into investigative custody in August last year. Prosecutors have repeatedly blocked bids by his lawyers to get him out of jail, saying they fear he could alter evidence or flee the country.
Steffi Graf has said she knew little about her financial affairs, entrusting them to her father from the start of a career which has taken her to the number one spot in women's tennis.
